MOVIMIENTO.description: Observable body displacement or change of position by the patient.
positive_examples: The patient walks, runs, or changes location.
negative_examples: The therapist moves while the patient remains still.

MOVIMIENTO_REPETITIVO.description: Repeated body movement by the patient with a recognizable recurring pattern.
positive_examples: The patient repeats the same rocking or hand movement.
negative_examples: A single isolated gesture without repetition.

CONTACTO_VISUAL.description: The patient directs their gaze toward another person or relevant object.
positive_examples: The patient's eyes are oriented toward the educator.
negative_examples: The face is turned away or the gaze target cannot be determined.

INTERACCION_OBJETO.description: The patient intentionally touches, manipulates, or uses a visible object.
positive_examples: The patient picks up or manipulates an object.
negative_examples: The object is visible but the patient does not act on it.

ORIENTACION_CORPORAL.description: The patient's torso or body is oriented toward a person, object, or activity.
positive_examples: The patient's torso turns toward the instrument.
negative_examples: Only another person's orientation is visible.

VOCALIZACION.description: A non-silent vocal sound produced by the patient without requiring verified speech content.
positive_examples: The patient produces an audible vocal sound.
negative_examples: The sound is music, an instrument, or an unidentified environmental noise.

HABLA.description: The patient produces discernible spoken language or speech-like verbal output.
positive_examples: Words or clearly speech-like utterances are audible from the patient.
negative_examples: Only instrumental sound or an unassigned voice is audible.

RISA.description: Laughter produced by the patient is audible in the window.
positive_examples: The patient's laugh is audible and attributable.
negative_examples: Laughter is absent or belongs to another person.

LLANTO.description: Crying or sobbing produced by the patient is audible in the window.
positive_examples: The patient's crying is audible and attributable.
negative_examples: Crying is absent or belongs to another person.

GRITO.description: A high-intensity vocal outburst produced by the patient is audible.
positive_examples: The patient emits an attributable shout or scream.
negative_examples: The loud sound is music, an instrument, or another person.

SILENCIO.description: No attributable patient vocal activity is detected during the complete reviewed window.
positive_examples: The patient remains vocally silent throughout the reviewed window.
negative_examples: An attributable patient vocalization occurs in the window.

ACTIVIDAD_MUSICAL.description: The patient produces or actively participates in an attributable musical sound.
positive_examples: The patient plays an instrument or sings as part of the activity.
negative_examples: Music is present but the patient is not the attributable source.

MIRADA.description: The patient looks toward a person or object as part of an observable interaction.
positive_examples: The patient looks at the educator during an exchange.
negative_examples: No interaction target can be identified.

GESTO.description: The patient makes an intentional communicative or expressive gesture.
positive_examples: The patient points, waves, nods, or uses another attributable gesture.
negative_examples: An involuntary or indeterminate movement without communicative context.

TACTO.description: The patient makes attributable physical contact with a person or object.
positive_examples: The patient touches the educator, peer, or object.
negative_examples: Contact belongs to another person or cannot be attributed.

IMITACION.description: The patient visibly reproduces a preceding movement, gesture, sound, or musical action.
positive_examples: The patient repeats an action immediately after the educator demonstrates it.
negative_examples: The action occurs without an identifiable preceding model.

RESPUESTA.description: The patient produces an observable response to a person, object, sound, or prompt.
positive_examples: The patient turns, gestures, vocalizes, or acts after a prompt.
negative_examples: No attributable response follows the stimulus.

ACTIVIDAD_CONJUNTA.description: The patient and another person participate in the same observable activity.
positive_examples: The patient and educator act on the same musical activity.
negative_examples: People are present but activities are unrelated.

INTERACCION_MUSICAL.description: The patient exchanges or coordinates musical actions with another participant.
positive_examples: The patient alternates, responds, or coordinates playing with the educator.
negative_examples: The patient is merely near an instrument without musical exchange.

INTERACCION_VERBAL.description: The patient participates in an attributable verbal exchange.
positive_examples: The patient answers, initiates, or responds verbally to another person.
negative_examples: Speech is absent, unassigned, or not part of an exchange.

positive_label_rule: An event overlaps the window and is either explicitly marked es_ejemplo=false without a source field, or belongs to an annotation file covered by a valid human approval record whose source hashes match.
negative_label_rule: A label is negative only inside a complete window covered by a done annotation task, which means all applicable modalities were reviewed.
exclusions: DEMUCA clinical scores are not targets in this task.
Example, machine-proposed, or unverified annotations are not labels.
This contract does not authorize model training or clinical use.
